title: Multiple testing and error rates
dek: m tests create a union of false-positive opportunities. Family-wise error and false-discovery rate are different operating characteristics. Name which one you bought.
story: One valid level-α test has P(false rejection) ≤ α under its null. m independent valid tests have P(at least one false rejection) = 1 − (1−α)^m ≈ mα when α is small. That is why a genome of unadjusted 0.05 stars is a random number generator.

Family-wise error rate (FWER) is P(V ≥ 1), V = number of false rejections. Bonferroni uses the union bound: each test at α/m, FWER ≤ α even under dependence. Šidák uses the independence formula. Holm is a stepwise FWER method that dominates Bonferroni.

False-discovery rate (next plate) is E[V/R | R>0] P(R>0), the expected fraction of rejections that are false. It is not a FWER. GWAS historically used a FWER-ish genome-wide threshold; RNA-seq and catalogue screens often use FDR. Mixing the names in a caption is a methods error.
deepTitle: Dependence, and what a p-value still is
deep: Positive dependence (LD, same isolates in every gene test) makes Bonferroni conservative: FWER < α. That is not a reason to unadjust; it is a reason that Westfall–Young permutation or a mixed-model null can buy power while keeping FWER.
A p-value remains P(T as or more extreme | this test’s H₀), not P(H₀ | data). Multiplicity adjustments change the rejection rule, not the definition of a single p.
Nested tests and sequential looks (interims) are another multiplicity. Bonferroni on 400,000 SNPs plus three interims plus five phenotypes is a stack. Pre-specify the family you are protecting.
Effect sizes and replication still matter. A Bonferroni-significant SNP with a tiny, batch-confounded effect is a small p, not a drug target.

example.title: 20 candidate resistance genes, unadjusted 0.05
example.setup: m = 20 valid tests, all null, independent, α = 0.05 each. What FWER did you actually run?

steps.title: Union
steps.body: P(at least one star) = 1 − 0.95^{20} ≈ 0.64. You did not run a 5% procedure; you ran a 64% procedure.

steps.title: Bonferroni
steps.body: Threshold 0.05/20 = 0.0025. FWER ≤ 0.05. Power at each gene drops; that is the bill.

steps.title: If you wanted discoveries not FWER
steps.body: BH FDR at 10% (next plate) is a different contract: among the genes you flag, you expect 10% to be false, not “64% chance of any error.”

example.takeaway: Define the family and the error rate. Unadjusted 0.05 across a screen is not a 5% study.

choices: The family-wise error rate via a union bound, at the price of power

check.prompt: On the multiple-testing small-multiples, E[V] grows with m while α% stays 5. The plate is saying:
choices: Unadjusted α=0.05 keeps the expected number of false rejections at 5% of m, which is not a FWER of 5%
check.answer: Unadjusted α=0.05 keeps the expected number of false rejections at 5% of m, which is not a FWER of 5%
check.why: E[V]=mα under all-null independent tests. FWER = P(V≥1) is already large when E[V] is large.

whyWrong.E[V] is a posterior: It is an expectation under the null simulation.
whyWrong.FWER equals E[V] always: One is a probability of any error, one is a count expectation.
